The main interface is not a chat window but a growing sheet of paper: human input, AI body text, thinking annotations, tool footnotes, and code transcriptions.

---

## What is this

**Lantai (兰台) is a Windows desktop Agent workbench** (Tauri 2 shell + TypeScript / React 19 frontend): a complete multi-Agent runtime.
The repo houses two product surfaces: the workbench (`src-ui/` + `src-tauri/`) and the engine (`engine/` and the `hologram-*` crates).

- **Canvas, not a message stream**: a session is a space. Multiple volumes lie on the same sheet, content can be pinned, dragged, and compared, and zooming changes the information granularity.
- **Multi-Agent runtime**: domain tool surface · sub-Agent pool (git worktree isolation) · Plan / Goal · memory and skills ·
  multi-vendor Provider · token governance.
- **Everything is a plugin**: panels / commands / tools / renderers / prompt segments / hooks / capabilities / swappable backends are all assembled through the contribution channel, and the factory-default state has no privileged rows.
- **Guardrails live in the shell, not in prompts**: permission engine · dangerous command interception · three-layer sandbox · encrypted credentials · permission gate auditing.
- **Ships with the HoloGram engine**: the code graph engine is a standalone process (a single Rust binary), off by default and enabled per workspace.
  It is also an independently consumable MCP server.

## Quick start

### 1. Install (Windows)

Download the installer (`.exe`) from [Releases](https://github.com/834063245-creator/LantaiAgent/releases), then launch it.
From source: run `build.cmd` in the repo root (it runs the frontend build first).

Settings → Apps → Lantai → Uninstall. The confirmation page has a "**Delete application data**" checkbox (unchecked by default). If you check it, the uninstaller also removes user-level data: `~/.lantai` (settings / global memory / skills / plugins and their data / old session backups), the legacy `~/.hologram` location, and the Lantai directories under `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (window state, WebView2 cache, encrypted API keys).

**Unchecked = no bytes deleted.** After reinstalling, everything continues as before. In-app auto-update also takes this uninstall path and never deletes data.
The `{project}/.lantai` directory inside your workspace (session text, attachments, canvas layout) belongs to your project files, and the uninstaller **does not** touch it.

## v1.3 changes (for Android 17 QPR2 / `CP4A.261105.040.A1`)

### System compatibility

- **Dual-signature compatibility for permission delegation cleanup**: Starting with Android 17, `IActivityManager.stopDelegateShellPermissionIdentity()` takes a UID-based signature instead.
  The old implementation would throw `NoSuchMethodError` at this point, even though the override had **actually been written successfully**, so the UI reported failure.
  At runtime, v1.3 tries the UID-based signature first, then falls back to the no-argument signature (see [pixel-volte-patch #472](https://github.com/kyujin-cho/pixel-volte-patch/issues/472), [PR #487](https://github.com/kyujin-cho/pixel-volte-patch/pull/487)).
- **Write / verify / cleanup separated into three states**: A cleanup failure no longer changes an already successful write into a failure; it is only shown as diagnostic information.
- **Per-SIM read-back verification**: After writing, the version fingerprint and key values are read back to confirm they actually landed in the configuration for that subId, rather than only checking whether the call threw an exception.
- **Build target raised**: `compileSdk` / `targetSdk` 35 → 36, version 1.2 → 1.3 (versionCode 4).
- **Build number and compatibility tiers**: The UI shows the system build number, security patch level, and the permission-delegation cleanup signature actually detected, and assigns a tier of: adapted / compatibility path / legacy system.

**A desktop plugin framework written in PySide6**

Chinese Version | [English Version](https://github.com/KKPIP-Tech/InstructionX/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md) | [French Version](https://github.com/KKPIP-Tech/InstructionX/blob/HEAD/README_FR.md) | [Russian Version](https://github.com/KKPIP-Tech/InstructionX/blob/HEAD/README_RU.md)

## What is InstructionX

InstructionX handles the parts of a desktop application that are not very exciting but that every tool has to deal with: plugin loading and unloading, configuration and data storage, background tasks, LLM, MCP, and a unified set of UI components. The specific tools built are determined by the plugins.

The current version is **Alpha 1.1.4**, and it runs on Windows 10/11 and macOS. The project is still under development, and interfaces may change. The framework runs from source code and is not distributed as a library.

## Key Features

- Hot loading, hot unloading, and hot reloading of plugins, with installation from GitHub or a local zip file, plus upgrades and downgrades via Releases.
- Multi-vendor LLM support, multiple sessions, tool calling, images and voice, Embedding, and usage statistics.
- MCP Server and MCP Client: they can expose plugin capabilities outward, and also connect to external MCP tools.
- SQLite WAL persistence, private/public data namespaces, and data change subscriptions.
- Normal, high-priority, and long-running tasks each use bounded thread pools, with support for scheduling, cancellation, and persistent recovery.
- Four interface languages, including Chinese and English, application-level font management, and a system tray.
- UIKit provides 59 components, 13 layouts, and 52 animations, plus charts, blueprints, a code editor, and Mermaid.
- Key non-UI plugin services can run in separate processes. By default they run in the same process, and isolation is not enforced.

Longado/ontopoc.description: Ontology tool for MCP / Claude: draft, check, and confirm ontologies from business data. Schema work ahead of a knowledge graph or semantic layer.
Longado/ontopoc.body:
OntoPoc is an ontology tool for a team's own data: the team writes down what its tables mean (object types, keys, code meanings, relations, views), code checks each definition against every row, a second named person confirms it on a given data version, and Q&A, boards and AI agents over MCP answer only from what was confirmed. It is not a knowledge-graph platform; it is the confirmed part of a semantic layer.

The team writes down what each table means: object types and primary keys, what each value of a code column means (for example, status code 2 = cancelled), relations, views (for example, "valid orders"), and derived attributes. This is the team's ontology, that is, the part of the semantic layer that answers "how is this number computed." Code checks each definition against all rows, and then another named colleague confirms it against a specific data version. Q&A, boards, and AI connected via MCP use only confirmed definitions. When data or a definition changes, anything that depends on it goes back to "needs review," and questions that use it are refused, with the item named and who can confirm it. OntoPoc is still in development, and no one other than its author is using it yet.

## How it refuses

There are three kinds of results. All of them run on the sample data included in the repository (150 orders, status codes 0–5). The [demo site](https://35-229-236-140.sslip.io/) (temporary address) uses the same data, and visitors have read-only access:

| You ask | OntoPoc answers | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "What is the total amount of valid orders?" | **119,810**, with a note beside it on how it was computed: view "valid orders" (paid, shipped, delivered), who confirmed it, based on orders version 1 | All definitions used have been confirmed |
| The question names a definition that no one has confirmed yet | Blocked before the model is queried, stating which definition it is and who can confirm it | Proposing is not confirming. People who can see this definition are told its name and who can confirm it. Viewers, who see only confirmed definitions, are not told the name of a definition that was never confirmed. For a confirmed definition awaiting re-confirmation, they are only told the answer is pending confirmation |
| After uploading `orders_update.csv` (which introduces new code 6, with no meaning written by anyone), the same question is asked again | Refused: "valid orders" needs review; the board shows who it is waiting on and the last figure | The data changed after confirmation |

When an answer covers all rows, the figures for each confirmed view are shown beside it. When an answer covers only one confirmed view, the figure for all rows is shown beside it. Which rows the figure above counts is decided the same way as before.

# ACE COMBAT 8 Interactive Music Player

On Windows, plays the *ACE COMBAT 8* soundtrack by the game's sections, loop points, and stems. The player remembers the last arrangement chosen for each track, supports switching stems by pass count and by bar, and allows manual queuing or immediate section switching in free arrangement.

## Android Phone Playback

The phone version uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Material 3 Expressive. arm64 phones running Android 8.0 or later can receive music, and x86_64 emulators can also run it. On first use, connect the phone and computer to the same local network.

1. Click the phone icon in the top-right corner of the computer app and select “Show connection QR code.” In the phone version under “Transfer,” scan the code, or enter the pairing code copied from the computer.
2. The phone first tries the computer's address on the same Wi-Fi subnet and sends back its local library. On the computer, select “Library” to choose arrangements track by track, or select “Playlist” to check individual tracks and arrangements already added to the playlist, or select all. When sending, only items checked in the current source are taken. Audio for the same song is sent only once, and the default arrangement is sent with the track. “Also transfer cockpit sound pack” can be checked separately.
3. After transfer, pick tracks from the phone's “Library.” You can listen to transferred arrangements directly, or choose “Free arrangement” to queue and switch sections in real time, switch sections immediately, adjust loops, and toggle stems. Music supports offline and lock-screen playback. The phone outputs 48 kHz stereo, and the computer sends PCM tracks that can be located by sample point. When you send a track that already exists, the phone reuses the existing audio and receives only the missing files and the selected arrangements.

The phone's library lists tracks by arrangement and indicates whether each one loops infinitely. Open “Now Playing” to see the full arrangement and the current step. The phone supports sequential playback, shuffle, playlist repeat, and single-track repeat. Items checked in the computer's “Playlist” and sent to the phone appear in the phone's “Computer Playlist” in their original order, and duplicate entries are kept. Sending from the playlist again updates this list. Tracks and arrangements already transferred can still be found under “All Tracks.”

The sandbox on the phone's playback page follows the music and cockpit sound actually being output. The center of the top bar controls playback. The gear icon in the top-left corner opens arrangement, stem, and cockpit sound settings, and the list icon in the top-right opens the queue and playback mode. Tap outside the panel or use the system back gesture to close it.

## Migrating Settings Between Computers

The phone icon in the top-right corner has “Export config JSON” and “Import config JSON.” The file contains all custom arrangements, playlist entries, order, and playback mode. Custom arrangements with the same ID under the same track, and playlist entries with the same ID, are updated, and content unique to this machine is kept. Default arrangements continue to use the version bundled with the player.

## Usage

Extract the ZIP completely, run `皇牌空战8音乐播放器.exe`, and confirm the Steam installation directory it finds automatically or choose it manually. By default, the player reads directly from the game and decodes only the current track and enabled sound effects temporarily. The “Settings” button in the top-right corner lets you change the directory, or extract audio for offline playback. The base soundtrack and cockpit sound effects take about 5.9 GiB, of which the online-mode soundtrack takes about 3.0 GiB. Choosing all native 7.1.4 assets adds about 3.9 GiB. The player prefers extracted files in the `audio` folder next to the program and reads from the game only when they are missing. Extracted assets can be moved along with the whole player directory.

boykush/dotfiles.body:
# dotfiles

Configuration files for a development environment centered on mise.

## Setup

You do not need to pre-install mise on a new environment. The `bin/mise` bundled in the repository (the self-installing wrapper output by `mise generate bootstrap`) fetches and runs the mise binary itself.

### 1. Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:boykush/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
cd ~/dotfiles
```

### 2. Machine setup (GUI apps, fonts, CLI tools, and dotfiles in one go)

```bash
./bin/mise bootstrap
```

`mise bootstrap` is a single command that runs declarative setup steps in order against the current config. In this repo, it applies all of the following at once: **GUI apps and fonts from `[bootstrap.packages]` (brew-cask; apps go to `/Applications`, fonts to `~/Library/Fonts`)**, **the dotfiles repository itself from `[bootstrap.repos]` (`~/dotfiles` tracks `main`)**, **CLI tools from `[tools]`**, and **symlinks and in-file block edits from `[dotfiles]`**. Other `[bootstrap.*]` sections are not defined, so they are no-ops. Declarative steps converge, so re-running is safe; you can check the status with `./bin/mise bootstrap status`.

## Version mapping (dsh-daemon ↔ dsh)

| dsh-daemon | Supported dsh | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1.35 | **0.1.x and 0.2.x** | Adds **uptime** to the health line of `status` / `dsh_daemon_status`: `Web server: ✅ healthy on 127.0.0.1:3080 (PID 90078) · up 2h 15m`. It is taken from this generation's `WEB_STARTED` (reset on every launch and adoption, so its age equals the process age). If the file is missing (early installs), it is not shown and no number is made up. Both places share the same `formatUptime()` and show two levels, chosen from `d`/`h`/`m`/`s` |
| 0.1.34 | **0.1.x and 0.2.x** | Fixes issue #9, “after a plugin upgrade auto-generates a new config, the install's port is not reused, causing an infinite restart loop”: after a package upgrade, plugin startup regenerates `watchdog.js` based on `GEN_VERSION`. That path passed `DEFAULT_PORT` (3080) as a placeholder to `discover()`, and in `discover()` an **explicitly passed portArg has the highest priority** (above `ctx.webServer.port`, `DSH_WEB_PORT`, and the default) ⇒ the generated file was written as `const PORT = 3080`, and `.daemon-port` was also overwritten to 3080. Users who installed on a non-default port were then watched by the watchdog on a port nobody was serving ⇒ always “unhealthy” ⇒ infinite restarts. Regeneration now first reads the `.daemon-port` written at install time and reuses it as-is. Only when that file is missing or unreadable (installs from earlier versions) does it hand off to `discover()` to infer the port from the running web server, instead of guessing 3080. **Affected installs need an explicit `dsh_daemon_reinstall port=<real port>`** |

# NukeApp-OSS

NukeApp-OSS is an Android Hook module for **Douyin** (`com.ss.android.ugc.aweme`). Once installed, a new entry "NukeApp-OSS" appears in Douyin's settings page. Opening it shows more than a hundred feature toggles, and changes take effect after Douyin restarts.

## What it can do

The settings page lists features by category. Only "Disable double-tap to like" is enabled by default. Everything else is off by default, so turn on whatever you need.

| Section | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| Video | Recommendation feed, playback control, video quality and cache, video page, gestures and actions, danmaku, ads |
| Social | Comments, messages, chat features, sharing and reposting, personal profile, privacy |
| App | Layout and display, usage time, app and system, other |

A few examples: not reporting read status (can apply only to conversations on a blacklist or whitelist), custom spark (huoxing streak) days (visible only to you), automatic streak continuation, automatic daily collection of Huoxing (once a day on a schedule, can be limited to selected friends), automatic red packet grabbing, chat message repeat (a "+1" beside the bubble), and removing the repost count limit. Every item has a one-sentence description on the settings page.

Besides the built-in features, you can import `.nks` script packages on the "Scripts" page of the settings and write your own features in JavaScript. For how to write and package scripts, see the [Script SDK](https://github.com/dartcv/NukeApp-OSS/blob/HEAD/sdk/script-sdk/README.md).

## Requirements

- Android 8.1 (API 27) or later.
- Douyin (not the international TikTok app).
- Choose one of the three methods below to get the module into Douyin. All three provide the same features. They differ only in how the module is loaded into the app:

| Method | Best for | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Xposed | Users already running a framework such as LSPosed | A framework that supports classic Xposed (API 82) or modern libxposed (API 102) |
| Zygisk | Rooted devices using Magisk, KernelSU, etc. | Zygisk enabled, and the device is `arm64-v8a` |
| Patching | Unrooted devices | Patch Douyin with NukePatcher. Android 9 or later, 4 KiB page size |

It is fine to enable several methods at once. Within a single process, only the first entry point to arrive takes effect, so hooks are never applied twice.

## Installation

### Step 1: Get the module APK

With the Xposed or Zygisk method, install the NukeApp-OSS APK on your phone. The settings page is part of that APK. With the patching method you don't install it. Just select this APK as a file in NukePatcher.

### Method 1: Xposed

1. Enable NukeApp-OSS in the framework, with the scope set to Douyin.
2. Fully restart Douyin (force stop it, then open it again).

# Crazy Water World · Voyage Console

  [](LICENSE)

Manage your Crazy Water World accounts on this machine. Connects directly to the game WebSocket to schedule reward claims, base management, hero development, and fleet missions. Supports independent per-account configuration, resource budgets, and runtime logs. Primarily targets Windows, with basic macOS runtime support.

[Quick Start](#快速开始) · [Features](#功能一览) · [Common Commands](#常用命令) · [Usage Guide](https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld/blob/HEAD/docs/console-guide.md) · [Changelog](https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

## Quick Start

### 1. Install the environment and download the project

Install **Node.js 22.12 or later** (also compatible with 20.x 20.19+) and Git, then reopen your terminal and run:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld.git
cd crazywaterworld
```

Alternatively, download the repository ZIP and extract it. The one-click startup script automatically checks and installs project dependencies. The project uses the npmmirror mainland China mirror by default via `.npmrc`, which applies to both one-click startup and manual installation.

### 2. Prepare the game protocol files (required)

The repository does not include the game protocol, and **the console cannot start without protocol files**. Choose one of the following:

- **Local WeChat cache**: In the desktop version of WeChat, fully enter Crazy Water World once, wait for the game to finish loading, then exit the game. The tool will automatically read the cache.
- **Your own protocol package**: Place `_src_chunks_.wxapkg` in the project root directory (same level as `package.json`) or in the `protocol/` subdirectory.

The local WeChat cache takes priority over your own package. If the latest WeChat package is missing subpackages or is corrupted, fully reload the game, or explicitly specify a usable protocol file with `CW_PROTO_BUNDLE`. [Specifying paths and macOS permission notes](https://github.com/xutongxue233/crazywaterworld/blob/HEAD/docs/console-guide.md#启动与排查)

WeChat QR login, Alipay login, and APP login also require protocol files to be prepared first. Configuration tables and the world map are automatically updated from the game CDN, but protocol files must still be provided using one of the methods above.

### 3. Start the console

**Windows:** Double-click `start-console.cmd` in the project root directory, or run the following in the terminal:

```powershell
.\start-console.cmd
```

# My OpenCode × DeepSeek Config

**Simplified Chinese** | [English](https://github.com/znlgis/my-opencode-deepseek-config/blob/HEAD/README.en-US.md)

**OpenCode v2 × DeepSeek optimal configuration**: under the OpenCode v2 multi-agent framework, this setup keeps only one model, `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, and uses thinking levels to divide the work among agents. Core principle: **token efficiency first, achieving the best development results at the lowest context cost**.

## Current configuration overview

- Default primary agent: `orchestrator`
- Only model: `deepseek/deepseek-flash` (V4.1 Flash, native multimodal). Agents are distinguished only by thinking level: default (thinking off) / `#low` / `#high` / `#max`
- Agent nesting depth: `experimental.subagent_depth: 2` (v2 native key; the v1 top-level `subagent_depth` was dropped by v2 and this repo no longer writes it. It exactly covers the deepest actual chain, `orchestrator → light-orchestrator → oracle`. All other subagents are forbidden from delegating, since deeper levels only add token overhead and amplify the attack surface)
- Session sharing: disabled (`share: "disabled"`)
- Permission baseline: `read` allowed by default; `shell` defaults to `ask` (unmatched commands always require manual confirmation; dangerous patterns are not enumerated). Sensitive `.env`-type files are `deny`; external directories are `ask`; read-only agents get shell rules (deny everything by default, allow only read-only subcommands). In v2.4.0, `browser` is globally `deny` (agents may not drive logged-in browsers), and `automations: false` (no background scheduled tasks)
